title: `OBJECT_CONSTRUCT` drops NULL fields
verdict: arrays equal elementwise; objects without their NULL fields
description: `ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(1, NULL) = ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(1, NULL)` is TRUE. `OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('a', 1, 'b', NULL)` drops `b`, so it equals `OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('a', 1)`, and `OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('a', NULL)` equals `{}`; `OBJECT_CONSTRUCT_KEEP_NULL` keeps them. Key order does not matter.
reference: Structs compare structurally, NULL fields equal. sverify refuses structs and lists on Snowflake.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT array_construct(1, 2) = array_construct(1, 2), array_construct(1, NULL) = array_construct(1, NULL), object_construct('a', NULL) = object_construct(), array_construct(1, 2) < array_construct(1, 3)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
